site.name: migration-atlas
site.summary: Migration Atlas — animal migration tracking (local demo) Fictional global animal-tracking atlas. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Page `index.html` — Atlas Three columns: left filter rail, center map + player, right inspector. The map is a hand-rolled SVG world (equirectangular projection) drawn from inline continent polygons and lon/lat graticules. Seven species are pre-loaded, each with a per-individual synthetic track of 12 monthly waypoints. Filters (left): species toggles with sample size counts, study year, display toggles (trail line, monthly position dots, stop-over polygons). Player (below map): slider scrubs through January → December. Play / pause button animates the season; speed selector controls cadence. As the slider advances, individuals' trails extend.

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full migration-atlas system, prioritizing the primary data visualization flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Migration Atlas has several UX issues: non-functional navigation links (About, Methods, Studies), unresponsive speed selector in mobile, small checkbox tap targets, missing feedback for Save/Cite buttons, and inconsistent study year dropdown. These impact usability, especially for mobile users and those needing navigation or feedback.

exploration_plan.goal: Critique the UX of the migration-atlas system, focusing on the primary data visualization flow (map, player, filters) and adjacent states/recovery paths.
exploration_plan.summary: Explore the index.html page in desktop and mobile viewports. Validate filter interactions, player functionality, map visualization, and recovery paths. Check small tap targets and responsive layout.
assumptions: Only index.html is present (no adjacent pages). Primary flow is filter → map → player interaction.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets (checkboxes, links) for mobile usability. Complex filter/player interaction state recovery.

phases.title: Filter Interactions (Desktop)
phases.objective: Validate species, year, and display filter functionality.
key_checks: Toggle species checkboxes (e.g., Western osprey, Monarch butterfly) and verify map updates.
Change study year via dropdown and verify map/player updates.
Toggle display checkboxes (Show trail, Show monthly positions, Show stop-over polygons) and verify map updates.
Use species search input to filter and verify results.
exit_criteria: All filter interactions update the map/player as expected.

phases.title: Player Functionality (Desktop)
key_checks: Scrub the month slider and verify map/individual stats update.
Click play/pause button and verify animation (trail extension, month update).
Change speed via selector (0.5×, 1×, 2×, 4×) and verify animation cadence.
Verify player resets correctly after filter changes.
exit_criteria: Player controls update the map/individual stats as expected.

phases.title: Map & Inspector (Desktop)
phases.objective: Validate map visualization and individual inspector interaction.
key_checks: Click a trail/dot/tag on the map and verify individual inspector updates.
Verify trail, monthly position, and stop-over polygon rendering based on display filters.
Check map responsiveness to filter/player changes (e.g., trail extension during animation).
Verify aggregate stats update with filter/player changes.
exit_criteria: Map and inspector interactions update correctly with filter/player actions.

phases.title: Responsive Layout (Mobile Viewport)
phases.objective: Validate responsive layout and mobile interactions.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport and verify responsive layout (column reflow, tap target sizes).
Repeat critical filter/player checks (e.g., toggle a species, scrub slider) in mobile view.
Check small tap targets (checkboxes, links) for usability (e.g., can they be tapped easily).
Verify map/player/inspector readability in mobile view.
exit_criteria: Mobile layout is usable, critical interactions work, and tap targets are acceptable.

phases.title: Recovery Paths & Edge Cases
phases.objective: Test state recovery and edge cases (e.g., all filters off, max speed, small species counts).
key_checks: Reset all filters (uncheck species, default year, hide all display) and verify map/player state.
Set player to max speed (4×) and scrub quickly; verify no errors/crashes.
Select a species with small count (e.g., Wandering albatross, n=4) and verify map rendering.
Test 'Cite this view' and 'Save view' buttons (even if dummy actions) for feedback.
exit_criteria: System recovers from extreme states, no errors, and buttons provide feedback.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise all visible controls (filters, player, map interactions, buttons) on index.html.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks (filters, player, map) in mobile viewport.

notes: Max steps (80) allow exhaustive exploration of the single page's controls and states.

findings.user_goal: Access 'About' or 'Methods' information via navigation links
findings.problem: Navigation links (About, Methods, Studies) are non-functional, only changing the URL to `index.html#` without displaying relevant content.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'About' link (target_id: ux-5) and 'Methods' link (target_id ux-4) resulted in no visible content update or navigation to a new page.
findings.why_it_matters: Users seeking information about the atlas or its methods cannot access it, reducing trust and usability.
findings.suggestion: Fix the links to navigate to relevant pages or display modal content with the information.

findings.user_goal: Adjust animation speed via the speed selector in mobile view
findings.problem: The speed selector in mobile view does not update to the selected speed (e.g., '2×'), remaining at the default or previous value.
findings.evidence: Attempts to select '2×' speed in mobile view failed; the speed selector remained at '0.5×' or '1×' despite interaction.
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile users cannot adjust animation cadence, limiting their ability to control the visualization speed.
findings.suggestion: Fix the speed selector's interaction logic to update the animation speed correctly in mobile view.

findings.user_goal: Toggle species or display checkboxes on mobile
findings.problem: Checkbox tap targets (e.g., species, display toggles) are 13x13px, below mobile guidance (44px), making them hard to interact with.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings highlight checkbox tap targets (13x13px) are below mobile guidance (44px), and the 'Play' button (26x40px) is also below guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile users may struggle to tap checkboxes accurately, leading to frustration and errors.
findings.suggestion: Increase checkbox and button tap targets to at least 44x44px for mobile usability.
findings.source_hint: index.html: ux-4, ux-5, ux-12, ux-13, ux-14

findings.user_goal: Receive confirmation after saving or citing a view
findings.problem: Buttons like 'Save view' and 'Cite this view' lack visible feedback (e.g., color change, animation, or text update) when clicked.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Save view' (ux-7) and 'Cite this view' (ux-6) resulted in no visible feedback or URL change.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot confirm if their action (saving/citing) was successful, leading to confusion and repeated actions.
findings.suggestion: Add visual feedback (e.g., button color change, success message) to confirm the action was executed.

findings.user_goal: Update the study year via the dropdown
findings.problem: The 'STUDY YEAR' dropdown does not update the map or aggregate stats when a new year is selected (e.g., '2024 season').
findings.evidence: After selecting '2024 season' from the dropdown, the visible text still showed 'Migration Atlas — 2025 season' and aggregate stats remained unchanged.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot explore migration data for different years, limiting the tool's functionality.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the dropdown updates the map and aggregate stats when a new study year is selected.

findings.user_goal: Interact with form fields (e.g., dropdowns, checkboxes)
findings.problem: A form field (dropdown) has no label, aria-label, or placeholder, violating accessibility standards.
findings.evidence: The 'STUDY YEAR' dropdown (target_id: ux-11) has no visible label or accessible name, as highlighted in layout warnings.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users cannot identify the purpose of the dropdown, reducing accessibility.
findings.suggestion: Add a label or aria-label to the dropdown to describe its purpose (e.g., 'Select study year').

gaps: 1 browser action(s) failed and should be retried or analyzed.
